name: Full Body Stretch
subtitle: Daily morning protocol · head to toe
source: Aaron's own routine sheet (morning_stretch_routine.html, added 2026-10-31). Seed data for E5 — not yet reviewed against the hypermobility rules in E5.
units: hold = seconds; perSide = do each side; reps = repetitions; sets = repeats of the hold

items.name: Neck Side Tilt
items.cue: Sit tall. Ear toward shoulder, let gravity do it — no pulling with the hands. Switch sides.

items.name: Neck Rotation
items.cue: Chin level, rotate to look over each shoulder. Hold at end range without forcing.

items.name: Chin Tuck
items.cue: Draw the chin straight back (not down). Hold 5 s, release.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cue: Inhale into cow, exhale into cat. Slowly, one vertebra at a time.
items.flag: Gentle — don't force thoracic extension past a comfortable range

items.name: Thoracic Extension over Rolled Towel
items.cue: Towel or foam roller across the upper back at the apex of the curve. Arms crossed or overhead. Move it up and down in small steps.
items.flag: Most important stretch in the routine for kyphosis — take your time

items.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
items.cue: Forearms on the frame at 90°, step through. Chin tucked. Try low, mid and high arm heights.

items.name: Thread the Needle
items.cue: Slide one arm under the body, rotate until the shoulder meets the floor. Breathe, switch.

items.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
items.cue: Pull the arm across with the other hand at the elbow. Keep the shoulder down.

items.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
items.cue: Hand behind head, other hand eases the elbow back. Ribs down.

items.name: Wrist Flexor & Extensor Stretch
items.cue: Arm out in front. Flexors: pull the fingers back. Extensors: push the fingers down. Both sides.

items.name: Supine Knee-to-Chest
items.cue: One knee in, other leg flat. Then both knees together, rock gently side to side.

items.name: Supine Spinal Twist
items.cue: Knee across the body, opposite arm out flat. Look away from the knee. Don't force the knee down.

items.name: Child's Pose
items.cue: Hips back to heels, arms forward. Walk the hands to each side for the lats.

items.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Lunge
items.cue: Back knee down, hips forward gently, torso upright, slight posterior pelvic tilt.
items.flag: Matters for the squat — tight hip flexors feed anterior pelvic tilt under load

items.name: Pigeon Pose (modified)
items.cue: Shin forward across the body, hips sink toward the floor, hands support. If too intense, do a lying glute stretch instead.

items.name: Butterfly Stretch
items.cue: Soles together, sit tall, elbows ease the knees down. Heels closer = more intense.

items.name: Deep Squat Hold
items.cue: Shoulder-width, toes slightly out, as deep as possible. Hold a doorframe or pole if needed. Elbows press knees out.
items.flag: Transfers directly to squat depth and hip stability

items.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
items.cue: Hold behind the thigh or calf, not the knee. Straighten as far as it goes; flex the foot for the calf.

items.name: Standing Forward Fold (progressive)
items.cue: Feet together, hang. Each exhale, straighten the legs a little more.

items.name: Seated Single-Leg Forward Fold
items.cue: One leg straight, other bent in. Reach toward the foot without rounding the lower back to cheat.

items.name: Standing Quad Stretch
items.cue: Foot to glute, knees together, stand tall. Use the wall — hypermobility.

items.name: Prone Quad Stretch
items.cue: Face down, pull one foot toward the glute. Hips stay down.

items.name: Standing Calf Stretch
items.cue: Back leg straight, heel down throughout.

items.name: Bent-Knee Calf Stretch
items.cue: Same position, back knee slightly bent — shifts it to the soleus.
items.flag: Tight soleus is a hidden limiter on squat depth

items.name: Ankle Circles & Toe Spreads
items.note: 10 circles each direction, then spread toes and hold 5 s
